    About this map

    A style study for the project's Bible maps, after Eilers Sunday School Map No. 3, Roman Empire and the Routes of the Travels of St. Paul (A. H. Eilers & Co., St. Louis), redrawn from open data.

    What we kept from Eilers

    • Flat tints for each province, with the seas left as paper
    • Water lines along the coasts, and hachured relief
    • Each journey in its own color, with the stops numbered
    • A "?" after places whose location is uncertain
    • A grid with an index of places keyed to it

    What we changed

    • Labels never overlap. More appear as you zoom in.
    • Type is never smaller than 11 pixels on screen
    • Borders are drawn as lines as well as tints, so they don't depend on color
    • Choose a journey to follow it stop by stop, with the verse for each stop

    How it was made

    • Land, water and relief come from elevation data; rivers are traced from it, and the Nile and the lakes come from Natural Earth.
    • The journeys follow Acts and Galatians. Every stop is named in the verse given, and the build checks each name against this project's translation. Sea passages keep to open water and land journeys to the easiest ground; both are pictures of the order of places, not of the exact way. Where Acts names only a region, the way through it is dashed.
    • Provinces are approximate, grown from their towns. Boundaries changed often in these years; the map shows them about AD 50.
    • Places are the towns named in Acts to Revelation that OpenBible.info can locate. Places scored below 500 out of 1,000 are marked "?".
    • Names are spelled as in this project's Open Plain English Translation.

    Sources

    • Places: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data, CC BY 4.0
    • Elevation: AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1)
    • Style: the Eilers Sunday School wall maps, published before 1931
    • Rivers and lakes: Natural Earth (public domain)
